primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Chronic inflammatory sacroiliitis and enthesitis in axial spondyloarthritis cause inflammatory back pain, progressive spinal stiffness, and reduced chest expansion, often associated with HLA-B27.
vignette: A 25-year-old man has 8 months of low back pain and morning stiffness that improve with exercise but not rest. Pelvic imaging shows bilateral sacroiliitis.
distractor_notes: Mechanical back pain generally worsens with activity and improves with rest.
Rheumatoid arthritis primarily affects peripheral synovial joints and usually spares the sacroiliac joints.
Polymyalgia rheumatica occurs in older adults with shoulder and hip girdle stiffness.
Osteoarthritis causes degenerative pain, not inflammatory sacroiliitis in a young adult.
key_expl: Young age, inflammatory back pain, and bilateral sacroiliitis are classic for ankylosing spondylitis.
objective: Recognize axial spondyloarthritis from inflammatory back pain and sacroiliitis.

sources.title: Ankylosing spondylitis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes inflammatory back pain and spinal stiffness in ankylosing spondylitis.

sources.title: Ankylosing Spondylitis
sources.support: NIAMS describes sacroiliac and spinal inflammation in ankylosing spondylitis.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Loss of self-tolerance leads to autoantibody formation against nuclear antigens and immune-complex deposition in multiple organs.
vignette: A 24-year-old woman has photosensitive malar rash, oral ulcers, inflammatory arthritis, proteinuria, and low complement levels.
lead: Which immunologic mechanism most directly contributes to tissue injury?
distractor_notes: IgE-mediated reactions cause immediate allergy, not multisystem lupus.
A microbial toxin does not explain autoantibodies and low complement.
Neutrophil adhesion failure causes immunodeficiency.
Receptor-stimulating antibodies are characteristic of diseases such as Graves disease, not the broad immune-complex injury of lupus.
key_expl: Many organ manifestations of SLE are mediated by autoantibody-containing immune complexes that activate complement and inflammation.
objective: Explain SLE tissue injury as a type III hypersensitivity process.

sources.title: Lupus
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes lupus as a systemic autoimmune disease affecting skin, joints, kidneys, and other organs.

sources.title: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
sources.support: NIAMS describes autoantibody and immune-mediated tissue injury in lupus.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Defective mineralization of mature osteoid, commonly from vitamin D deficiency, produces bone pain and weakness with low phosphate or calcium and elevated alkaline phosphatase.
vignette: A 58-year-old woman with severe vitamin D deficiency has diffuse bone pain, proximal muscle weakness, low phosphate, and elevated alkaline phosphatase.
lead: Which bone abnormality is most likely present?
distractors: Excessive osteoclast resorption with normal mineralization only
Failure of type I collagen synthesis
Dense brittle bone from osteoclast failure
distractor_notes: Osteoporosis has reduced bone mass but normal mineralization.
Type I collagen defects cause osteogenesis imperfecta.
Osteoclast failure causes osteopetrosis.
Malignant osteoid production occurs in osteosarcoma.
key_expl: Osteomalacia is impaired mineralization of adult bone matrix.
objective: Differentiate osteomalacia from osteoporosis by the mineralization defect.
clues: bone pain with elevated alkaline phosphatase

sources.title: Osteomalacia
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes osteomalacia as softening of adult bone due to defective mineralization.

sources.title: Vitamin D
sources.support: NIH ODS describes vitamin D deficiency as a cause of osteomalacia in adults.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Defective osteoclast-mediated bone resorption produces abnormally dense but brittle bone and can narrow marrow spaces, causing fractures, anemia, and cranial nerve compression.
vignette: A child has recurrent fractures, anemia, and visual impairment. Radiographs show diffusely increased bone density.
lead: Which cell type is primarily dysfunctional?
distractor_notes: Osteoblasts form bone and are not the primary defective cell in classic osteopetrosis.
Chondrocytes drive cartilage growth but not the generalized dense-bone phenotype.
Fibroblasts produce connective tissue.
Neutrophils do not regulate bone resorption.
key_expl: Osteopetrosis results from impaired osteoclast bone resorption.
objective: Connect diffuse increased bone density with osteoclast dysfunction.
clues: marrow failure and cranial nerve compression

sources.title: Osteopetrosis
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes defective osteoclast bone resorption causing dense but fragile bones.

sources.title: Bone Diseases
sources.support: NIAMS describes normal bone remodeling and the roles of osteoclasts and osteoblasts.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Ewing sarcoma is a malignant small round cell tumor of bone, often caused by EWSR1-FLI1 fusion, typically arising in the diaphysis of long bones or pelvis in children and adolescents.
vignette: A 14-year-old boy has fever and increasing thigh pain. Imaging shows a destructive diaphyseal femoral lesion with an onion-skin periosteal reaction.
distractor_notes: Osteosarcoma more often occurs in the metaphysis and can show a sunburst pattern.
Osteoid osteoma is a small benign lesion with nocturnal pain relieved by NSAIDs.
Giant cell tumor typically arises in the epiphysis after skeletal maturity.
Chondrosarcoma usually affects older adults.
key_expl: A painful diaphyseal bone tumor with onion-skin periosteal reaction in an adolescent is classic Ewing sarcoma.
objective: Differentiate Ewing sarcoma from osteosarcoma by age, location, and radiographic pattern.

sources.title: Ewing sarcoma
sources.support: NCI describes Ewing sarcoma as a childhood and adolescent bone cancer often involving long bones and pelvis.

sources.title: Ewing sarcoma
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes Ewing sarcoma as a malignant bone tumor in children and young adults.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: UV-induced DNA damage and Hedgehog pathway dysregulation drive a locally invasive keratinocyte cancer that rarely metastasizes.
vignette: A 68-year-old man has a slowly enlarging pearly papule with telangiectasias and a rolled border on the nose.
distractor_notes: Squamous cell carcinoma more often appears as a scaly or keratotic plaque or nodule.
Melanoma is a melanocytic malignancy with pigment asymmetry and evolution.
Seborrheic keratosis is a benign waxy stuck-on lesion.
Actinic keratosis is a rough premalignant lesion.
key_expl: A pearly telangiectatic papule with a rolled border on sun-exposed skin is classic basal cell carcinoma.
objective: Recognize basal cell carcinoma from its characteristic morphology.

sources.title: Basal cell skin cancer
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes basal cell carcinoma as a common skin cancer with pearly or shiny lesions.

sources.title: Skin Cancer
sources.support: NCI describes basal cell carcinoma as a common UV-associated skin malignancy.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Cumulative UV exposure causes keratinocyte DNA damage and malignant transformation, often arising from actinic keratoses on sun-exposed skin.
vignette: A 74-year-old farmer has a firm scaly ulcerated nodule on the dorsal hand arising from a long-standing rough keratotic lesion.
distractor_notes: Basal cell carcinoma is usually pearly with telangiectasia rather than a keratotic ulcerated nodule.
Melanoma is a melanocytic lesion with pigment and asymmetry features.
Dermatofibroma is a benign firm papule.
Psoriasis causes multiple inflammatory plaques rather than a solitary invasive nodule.
key_expl: An ulcerated keratotic nodule arising from actinic damage on sun-exposed skin is characteristic of SCC.
objective: Recognize cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma arising from actinic keratosis.

sources.title: Squamous cell skin cancer
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma as a sun-associated keratinocyte cancer.

sources.title: Skin Cancer
sources.support: NCI describes squamous cell carcinoma and UV exposure as a major risk factor.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Autoimmune destruction of melanocytes causes sharply demarcated depigmented macules and patches with preserved skin texture.
vignette: A 29-year-old woman with autoimmune thyroid disease develops symmetric sharply demarcated depigmented patches on the hands and around the mouth.
lead: Loss of which cell type most directly causes the lesions?
distractor_notes: Keratinocytes remain present and normal in vitiligo.
Langerhans cells are antigen-presenting cells and are not the lost pigment-producing population.
Fibroblasts synthesize dermal matrix.
Merkel cells participate in touch sensation.
key_expl: Vitiligo results from destruction of epidermal melanocytes and loss of melanin production.
objective: Connect autoimmune depigmentation with melanocyte loss.

sources.title: Vitiligo
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes vitiligo as loss of skin pigment due to destruction of pigment-producing cells.

sources.title: Vitiligo
sources.support: NIAMS describes autoimmune destruction of melanocytes in vitiligo.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Rapid bacterial spread along fascial planes causes thrombosis, tissue necrosis, systemic toxicity, and pain often disproportionate to early skin findings.
vignette: A 55-year-old man with diabetes develops rapidly worsening leg pain after a small skin injury. Pain is severe out of proportion to examination; within hours, swelling, bullae, and systemic hypotension develop.
distractor_notes: Cellulitis generally progresses less explosively and pain is proportionate to local findings.
DVT causes swelling and pain but not bullae, rapidly spreading necrosis, and septic shock.
Gout causes acute joint inflammation, not fascial tissue destruction.
Contact dermatitis is superficial and pruritic rather than deeply painful and toxic.
key_expl: Rapid progression, pain out of proportion, bullae, and systemic toxicity are red flags for necrotizing fasciitis.
objective: Recognize necrotizing soft-tissue infection from early high-risk clinical features.
clues: rapid progression with bullae and shock

sources.title: Necrotizing fasciitis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes rapidly progressive fascial infection with severe pain and systemic illness.

sources.title: About Necrotizing Fasciitis
sources.support: CDC describes necrotizing fasciitis as a rapidly spreading life-threatening soft-tissue infection.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Skin-barrier dysfunction and type 2 immune responses promote chronic pruritic eczematous inflammation, often associated with asthma and allergic rhinitis.
vignette: A 6-year-old child with asthma has recurrent intensely pruritic flexural eczema and dry skin.
lead: Which pathophysiologic abnormality best contributes to this disorder?
distractor_notes: Collagen loss causes connective-tissue fragility, not eczema.
Desmosomal autoantibodies cause pemphigus vulgaris.
Urate crystals cause gout.
Melanocyte destruction causes vitiligo.
key_expl: Atopic dermatitis is strongly linked to epidermal barrier dysfunction and allergic inflammation.
objective: Explain atopic dermatitis through skin-barrier failure and atopic immune activation.

sources.title: Atopic dermatitis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes eczema as a chronic pruritic inflammatory skin condition associated with dry skin and atopy.

sources.title: Atopic Dermatitis
sources.support: NIAMS describes skin-barrier and immune dysfunction in atopic dermatitis.
